results.text: Dawn Ward was charged with racially aggravated assault after a man at Euston station accused her of a racist slur. Dawn says she never said a word of it. Her lawyer didn't think she would go to jail, but warned her the worst case was jail. When she told her children what she was charged with, her youngest daughter Aston was 10. Aston asked if prison would let her out at least once a week to see them, or if she would come home every day. Dawn told her she wouldn't go to prison, because she didn't want her daughter worrying. That question made her want to fight more than ever. The case hung over her for two years, and a trial meant to last three days ran to nine. In the end all 12 jurors found her not guilty, and they waited outside the gates to tell her she should never have been in that courtroom.

"It changed just working with Elon. At my previous company, it was like, you never blow up a rocket engine or fail a rocket engine. That's bad. This is bad karma. Never test, always have a lot of margin and make sure that you don't fail it."

"You're watching it on, like, a fucking dozen screens as it's flying over Australia, as it goes into the darkness of night on the dark side of the planet, and then it comes over on the other side into the brightness of the sun and then lands in the ocean. It was bananas."

"But they have all these sensors all over the thing, and so they're monitoring the hull, and the hull actually had a problem. It was leaking. So they're like, 'Well, might explode. Might explode.' results.text:
Elon Musk quickly impressed Franz von Holzhausen, persuading him to join Tesla and leave behind a successful career at Mazda. Franz recalls: "For somebody who's going to put rockets into space, car is actually not that hard, and his vision for the car and his sustainable direction and message is exactly what I'm looking for."

In the summer of 2008, Franz already had the kind of automotive career most designers dream about, having penned sports cars at GM and led design at Mazda North America, while Tesla was near bankruptcy. 

But after meeting Elon Musk at SpaceX and going for a drive together in an early Roadster while people on the street stopped to stare, Franz walked away from his secure job to start designing the Model S from a blank sheet of paper. When he later explained why he took that leap of faith into a startup with no guarantees, his answer came down to Elon's total commitment: "Tesla was all in."
